podcast.title: Critical Reception
podcast.body: Critics are expected to be biased due to Lee Amgala Gheri's controversial nature, past conflicts within the music industry, and numerous enemies in music criticism. This bias was previously observed with some BDI material, which was reportedly unfairly criticized despite its quality. "Liam Gallagher es una persona muy polémica que ha tenido bastantes peleas y enemistades con gente importante de la industria musical y que tiene grandes enemigos en la crítica musical y muchas revistas no creo yo personalmente que vayan a ser muy objetivos haciendo la crítica de este disco."

podcast.title: Overall Quality
podcast.body: This album is praised for its ability to avoid sounding repetitive, long, or monotonous, with many unreleased tracks proving more potent than the singles. It features strong songs like "El Bold" and "El iPhone 9" and has no weak points or filler tracks, making it easy to listen to on repeat. The distinct voice of Lee Amgala Gheri, however, makes it difficult to separate the album's sound from his past work with Oasis. "el álbum no llega un punto en el que ni se te hace repetitivo ni se te hace largo ni siquiera tienen ningún punto bajo en el que te vengan a ser una canción hacia adelante porque parezca de relleno."

podcast.title: Production and Collaboration
podcast.body: The album's production involved notable figures, with Greg Castin contributing significantly as a producer and instrumentalist, assisting Lee Amgala Gheri in recording, composition, and overall musical support. Dan Grets also played a major role in the album's production, providing expertise as a respected sound engineer to ensure high-quality sound. Despite Lee Amgala Gheri being the primary artistic force, he shared songwriting rights and ownership with all the supporting musicians and personnel, showcasing a collaborative approach. "aunque este disco es de Liam Gallagher sus canciones están firmadas por mucha gente aunque Liam Gallagher ha tenido la idea principal del disco y eso el principal compositor y realmente artífice artístico del disco él ha compartido los derechos y la titularidad de las canciones con todos los músicos y la gente que le ha dado soporte lo cual realmente es bastante loable."

podcast.title: Self-Review (11/10)
podcast.body: Lee Amgala Gheri himself reviewed his entire discography for NME magazine, assigning incredibly high scores to his works. He rated Oasis's "Definitely Maybe" and "Morning Glory" a perfect 10 out of 10, but gave his own solo album an unprecedented 11 out of 10. "él le apuntó con un 11 sobre 10 a su propio trabajo en solitario."

podcast.title: Sound and Influences
podcast.body: The album is remarkably consistent and well-produced, avoiding an outdated 90s sound often feared from artists of that era. It is considered the most updated-sounding work from the Gallagher brothers since Oasis, including BDI and Noel Gallagher's solo efforts which still carried remnants of 90s Britpop and Oasis's classic sound. The album draws clear influences from The Beatles, 60s rock, Lof (likely The Kinks), and The Rolling Stones, often transporting listeners to that era, yet maintaining a fresh and contemporary feel. "no es un disco que suene viejo que suene noventero o que suene un tanto despasado que siempre el miedo que tenemos cuando esos artistas de los 90 tan marcados sacan material casi 20 años después de su época dorada."
